confirmed.statement: The total is 74 people: 'Participants were seventy-four second-year undergraduates enrolled in the Bachelor of Music programme at a university in South Korea.' The abstract gives the same 74, split n = 36 and n = 38.

confirmed.statement: Arm sizes at assignment match the form (36 and 38). The paper says 'participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups', then gives the experimental group as n = 36 and the control group as n = 38. The same paragraph says the random assignment 'was conducted at the class level' and gives no number of classes. That is a criterion-1 question. The count of people assigned does not depend on it.
Arm sizes at analysis match the form (36 and 38). Table 6 prints N = 36 (experimental) and N = 38 (control) for both the creativity and the analytical adjusted means.

The printed degrees of freedom fit 74 people analyzed. Levene's F(1, 72) = 1.284 and 0.916 reproduce the printed p = .261 and .342 (74 people minus 2 groups). Table 5 df2 = 69 is 74 minus 5 parameters (intercept, group, three covariates). Table 4 df2 = 68 is 69 - 2 + 1 for a one-df effect on two outcomes.
confirmed.locator: p. 9, RQ2, assumption checks; p. 11, Table 4; p. 12, Table 5

confirmed.statement: The paper has one study, so no person is counted in two studies. The growth models, the MANCOVA, and the cross-lagged models use the same 74 students. The epistemic network and Markov analyses use the experimental group only (Table 8, N = 36), and the form does not code them as outcomes.

The same students took part in another paper, Zhou and Kim (2024): 'These students were drawn from the cohort involved in our earlier study on the short-term effects of ChatGPT-4 (Zhou & Kim, 2024)'. The introduction describes that study as having 74 undergraduate music students in Korea. The form's sample_overlap records this. That paper (doi 10.1007/s10639-024-12705-z) is not in candidates.json and not in the learning dataset (dist/releases/2026-10-05.1/data/papers.csv), so no other atlas record counts these students.

confirmed.statement: Criterion 2 holds on S1 alone: 74 people analyzed across the two arms (36 + 38), above the threshold of 50.

Caveat, not an error in the counts: several other printed statistics are internally inconsistent, so they cannot confirm or contradict any sample size. Table 4 prints the Group Pillai's trace as .047 with F(2, 68) = 3.982, but a trace of .047 implies F of about 1.68, and F = 3.982 implies a trace of about .105. The Week 1 rows do not match either. The Table 5 eta-squared values back out df2 of about 68, not the printed 69. Table 2 prints RMSEA = .021 with chi-square = 885.330 on 78 df, which would give about .38 at N = 74. The Table 6 standard errors (0.18 and 0.17) cap the creativity group F at about 2.1 (2.4 with rounding), against the printed 7.216. None of this changes the printed head count of 36 + 38.
confirmed.locator: p. 6, Table 2; p. 11, Table 4; p. 12, Tables 5 and 6

summary: The PDF supports every participant count in the c148 form: 74 second-year music students were assigned, 36 to ChatGPT-4 and 38 to traditional instruction (p. 5; Abstract), Table 6 analyzes the same 36 and 38, the Levene and MANCOVA degrees of freedom fit 74 people, and 86 programme students minus 12 pilot-only students equals 74, with no withdrawal reported. Criterion 2 holds on this one study, and three caveats leave the counts unchanged: class-level assignment with an unstated number of classes is a criterion-1 question, the same students also took part in Zhou and Kim (2024), which no atlas record uses, and several other statistics in Tables 2, 4, 5, and 6 are internally inconsistent.
